technology_and_technique.topic: Targeted Lung Denervation (TLD) – patient selection and imaging criteria
technology_and_technique.summary: Candidates: COPD with ≥2 moderate exacerbations in the past 12 months requiring antibiotics or corticosteroids; includes chronic bronchitis and emphysema phenotypes on optimal medical therapy. Exclusions: asthma; exacerbations driven by persistent bacterial colonization; significant gastrointestinal comorbidities. Preprocedure CT required to confirm treatable bronchial anatomy and to exclude severe emphysema (>50% emphysema index at HU −950).
technology_and_technique.reference: Chapter text, Section 2.2; imaging criteria in Section 2.2

technology_and_technique.topic: Targeted Lung Denervation (TLD) – procedural technique and safety design
technology_and_technique.summary: One-session bronchoscopy under general anesthesia using a dual-cooled radiofrequency catheter connected to a console with a peristaltic pump that circulates coolant to the balloon tip to minimize bronchial injury. Device has CE mark (Europe, 2016). Specific complication rates and success percentages not reported in provided text.

Small pilot data suggest reductions in airway remodeling and inflammation based on cytokine analyses from bronchial wash/brush. No randomized comparative effectiveness data, safety event rates, or exacerbation reduction percentages reported in the provided excerpt.

technology_and_technique.topic: Bronchial Rheoplasty – mechanism, selection, and technique overview
technology_and_technique.summary: Mechanism: non-thermal pulsed electrical energy ablates goblet cells to reduce mucus hypersecretion. Target population: chronic bronchitis phenotype with persistent symptoms despite optimal medical therapy. Procedural details not fully provided in the excerpt. No yield percentages, safety rates, or comparative data reported in the provided text.

technology_and_technique.topic: Spray Cryotherapy (Metered Cryospray) – mechanism, selection, and technique overview
technology_and_technique.summary: Mechanism: precise-dose liquid nitrogen at −196 °C to freeze goblet cells, aiming to reverse goblet cell hyperplasia, reduce sputum, and improve quality of life. Target population: chronic bronchitis phenotype. Procedural specifics and outcomes not detailed in the excerpt. No yield or safety percentages reported.

technology_and_technique.topic: Technology comparison – Rheoplasty vs Spray Cryotherapy for chronic bronchitis
technology_and_technique.summary: Both target goblet cell hyperplasia in chronic bronchitis. Energy modality differs: pulsed electrical energy (rheoplasty) versus liquid nitrogen cryospray at −196 °C (spray cryotherapy). The excerpt provides no head-to-head trials, comparative safety, or efficacy percentages.

technology_and_technique.topic: Performance and selection tips applicable across modalities
technology_and_technique.summary: Careful phenotype-based selection is emphasized. For TLD: confirm anatomy via CT and exclude severe emphysema; avoid asthma and infection-driven exacerbators or those with significant GI comorbidities; perform under general anesthesia; use coolant-circulated RF balloon to limit airway injury. For chronic bronchitis therapies (rheoplasty and spray cryotherapy): select patients with persistent symptoms despite optimal medical therapy. No quantified procedural performance metrics reported.
